title: investigate a deployment-related availability incident
input: The incident owner supplies the affected application, incident window and approved telemetry connections.
action: DevOps Agent investigates available operational evidence and connected system context to identify likely causes and remediation guidance. Evidence access and permitted integrations bound the investigation.
output: The on-call engineer reviews the diagnosis against deployment history and applies an independently approved repair.
check: Compare the diagnosis with actual request failures and verify recovery before closing the incident.

title: carry a live contribution feed to the broadcast pipeline
input: A broadcaster supplies a licensed live contribution stream using the agreed transport and redundancy design.
action: MediaConnect receives and distributes configured live video flows to permitted outputs or entitled subscribers. It transports the contribution feed; downstream encoders create delivery renditions.
output: MediaLive consumes the delivered contribution stream and encodes the channel's streaming outputs.
check: Test source failover, receiving endpoint permissions and continuity under transport loss.

title: encode a live sports channel into adaptive renditions
input: The broadcaster supplies primary and backup live inputs and channel encoding settings.
action: MediaLive encodes the input into configured video, audio and caption outputs. Channel pipelines and input switching preserve the selected live workflow; output settings match the downstream packager.
output: MediaPackage receives the encoded streams and packages them for adaptive playback through the delivery CDN.
check: Check rendition playback, captions, input-switch continuity and aligned audio before the live event.

title: package encoded live video for adaptive players
input: The player requests a channel manifest while the broadcaster supplies encoded live segments.
action: MediaPackage ingests supported encoded streams and exposes configured playback endpoints and manifests. Packaging and content-protection settings determine the delivered formats; the encoder supplies the source renditions.
output: The CDN caches permitted manifests and segments and the player selects a rendition for its connection.
check: Verify manifest availability, segment timing, playback authorization and the intended live window.

title: personalize advertising in a streaming session
input: The video player starts a playback session with the permitted viewer and ad-request context.
action: MediaTailor obtains ad decisions from the configured ad decision server and stitches appropriate ad media into the session's manifest. The underlying content origin supplies the program stream.
output: The player follows the personalized manifest and reports playback events under the selected reporting mode.
check: Test ad-decision timeout, unfilled breaks, manifest continuity and tracking without exposing personal data.

title: match customer records across two permitted datasets
input: The data owner selects customer datasets, matching fields and the authorized result destination.
action: Entity Resolution applies the configured rule-based or supported matching workflow to the input records and assigns match groups. Matching confidence and chosen fields govern deduplication, not an automatic assertion of identity.
output: The analyst reviews matched groups before updating the master customer dataset.
check: Test known matches, near duplicates and false positives; retain source identifiers for reconciliation.

title: receive a satellite downlink during a scheduled contact
input: The mission operator prepares satellite registration, antenna requirements and the authorized contact window.
action: Ground Station coordinates the configured antenna contact and delivers received satellite data through the selected dataflow endpoint. Mission software performs payload decoding and application interpretation.
output: The ground processing application decodes the received payload and stores validated observation products.
check: Reconcile contact timing, delivered bytes and payload integrity; schedule recovery for missed observations.

title: respond to an account-specific scheduled service event
input: The operations team selects account events and the resources named by an upcoming AWS maintenance notice.
action: Health Dashboard shows relevant AWS service events and affected resources. Operators use the event's status, time and prescribed action to plan their response; dashboard viewing does not repair the workload.
output: The resource owner schedules the required update or evacuation and records affected workload ownership.
check: Verify the actual resource action and application health; an event marked closed does not establish business recovery.

title: query normalized clinical records in a FHIR datastore
input: A healthcare integration supplies authorized FHIR records and validates required patient and encounter identifiers.
action: HealthLake stores healthcare data in its configured FHIR datastore and serves permitted FHIR operations. Supported import and analytics integrations prepare clinical datasets under the configured authorization boundary.
output: The clinical application retrieves permitted patient resources or the analyst uses an approved analytical export.
check: Validate FHIR conformance, patient access restrictions and reconciliation with the source clinical system.

title: draft a clinician-reviewed note from a consultation recording
input: An authorized clinical workflow submits an approved consultation audio recording.
action: HealthScribe generates a transcript and preliminary clinical documentation with evidence references from the conversation. Generated documentation is a draft requiring professional review before entering the medical record.
output: The clinician checks each relevant statement against transcript evidence, edits the note and approves the final record.
check: Test speaker attribution and unsupported statements; verify consent, recording access and deletion policy.
